transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE) — Maria Velasquez (CISO, Argentum), Tom Hargreaves (Head of Platform), Raj Patel (Compliance), Ellen Cho (SRE)

[00:00] Jared: Hi everyone, thanks for making time today, appreciate it. quick round-robin? we can start with a 5 minute context then Priya will do a slightly deeper tech mapping.
[00:08] Maria: Hi, Maria here. we're doing a review across cloud vendors for LLMs, main concerns are residency for EU clients and auditability — must fit our internal financial regs.
[00:15] Tom: Tom — platform. we run most workloads in eu-west-1 and need to avoid logs leaving the region. also curious on dedicated vs private trade offs.
[00:22] Raj: Raj, compliance. we need to understand retention windows, redaction capabilities, and whether logs can be turned off for certain tenants.
[00:29] Priya: Awesome. quick product map — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem). switching between modes is possible but there are trade-offs. today we'll focus on residency+logs.
[00:42] Liam: quick note, some words might be transcribed odd, e.g. K V cache becomes K V cache in transcript.
[00:49] Maria: that's fine. start with your recommended pattern for EU-only processing, what's the simplest?
[00:53] Priya: For EU-only, simplest for speed-to-value is Hosted with region locking — we can route requests to eu-west-1 only, process and store telemetry there. However, Hosted by default keeps some telemetry in our control plane for billing and monitoring, which we can minimize. The stricter pattern is Dedicated in eu-west-1 — dedicated hardware in that region, logs can be configured to either forward to your S3 or to a customer-managed KMS for encryption. Private gives you the most control (VPC or on-prem) but requires longer lead times.
[01:22] Raj: When you say "minimize" telemetry, can you be explicit — do you store raw request/response pairs?
[01:30] Priya: Right, great question. We do have config flags: by default Hosted keeps aggregated metrics and short-lived request traces for debugging for up to 30 days. Raw request/response pairs are retained for 14 days for debugging then purged, unless you opt into exports. For Dedicated you can turn off raw retention and only export structured telemetry to your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS keys. On Private, you control all logs fully.
[01:56] Ellen: Are there options for on-the-fly redaction before logs are written? we need PII tokens removed from transcripts before hitting any persistent store.
[02:04] Priya: Yes, we offer a pre-log hook for scrubbers; you can run a custom lambda-style filter in the request path that redacts patterns (account numbers, ssn-like strings) before any persistence. On Dedicated we can run that within the same network so data never leaves. On Hosted there is a managed scrubber but for high assurance we recommend Dedicated/Private with your own scrubber.
[02:29] Tom: Key residency — do you support customer-managed keys? our policy requires keys be in our EU KMS and not accessible by Redwood staff.
[02:36] Jared: short answer: yes, for Dedicated and Private. You can either bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) where Redwood encrypts model cache and persisted data with your key—often integrated with AWS KMS/HSM— or in Private we can do local HSM/KMS. Hosted has limited BYOK capability today; we use envelope encryption and can arrange restricted-access keys for enterprise plans but it requires review.
[03:02] Raj: how about export controls — if we request an audit trail showing access to keys or decryption events, is that available?
[03:09] Priya: We emit audit logs for key usage; for Dedicated/Private you can ingest a copy into your SIEM. Those logs show key-id, timestamp, operation, and a request id. We can redaction-proof the logs, but we usually don't include full plaintext data.
[03:27] Maria: Schrems II and DP framework implications — we prefer EU-only processing for EU customers, no US analytics copies. Does Redwood offer region lock with zero cross-border telemetry?
[03:37] Priya: Yes, we offer region locking and the option to disable cross-region analytics. For enterprise Dedicated/Private we can guarantee control-plane separation per contract — the legal agreement includes commitments. Hosted has more managed telemetry and we may need a contractual addendum to prevent certain cross-border flows.
[03:57] Ellen: On retention windows: our policy is max 7 days raw and then only aggregate metrics for 365 days. can you do that?
[04:05] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated we can set raw retention to 7 days and export aggregated metrics to your S3 bucket for long-term storage. For Hosted we can approximate but there are agent-level traces kept for longer in some failure cases—so we recommend Dedicated for strict SLAs.
[04:22] Maria: PCI/HIPAA — we are not handling PHI but we do process payment-related metadata. do you have a HIPAA program?
[04:29] Jared: Redwood has a HIPAA compliance program for Enterprise customers; we can sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted can be covered on a case-by-case basis if we scope the usage and have additional controls.
[04:44] Raj: Encryption in transit — TLS ok — but mutual TLS between our infra and yours?
[04:49] Priya: mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private endpoints. Hosted supports TLS with token-based auth and IP allowlists; mTLS requires dedicated endpoints.
[04:59] Tom: Network-wise — can we VPC peering or private link? we want no public internet egress for inference traffic.
[05:06] Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink to avoid internet egress. Private is the same but you fully manage the network. Hosted cannot do peering but supports private endpoints for enterprise customers in some regions.
[05:20] Maria: On-showing evidence to auditors — what artifacts do you provide?
[05:24] Jared: SOC 2 report, encryption diagram, key usage logs, access lists, and operational runbooks. We'll share a redacted sample of audit logs showing access patterns.
[05:34] Raj: Is there a way to split tenancy so EU accounts are fully isolated to a Dedicated cluster while US accounts live on Hosted? we might prefer a hybrid approach.
[05:43] Priya: Absolutely, routing policies can send tenant traffic to different deployment modes. You can pin EU tenant IDs to a Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 and have US tenants on Hosted; the routing layer enforces that. Fallbacks are configurable — e.g., if Dedicated capacity is saturated you could fail closed or route to a restricted fallback.
[06:02] Ellen: About logs: we want redaction and partial hashing for tokens — do you support token hashing instead of storing plain redacted values?
[06:10] Priya: Yes, we can hash identifiers with a salted HMAC and store the digest only, so you can correlate without exposing PII. The salt can be customer-managed in your KMS for Dedicated/Private.
[06:22] Tom: Any compliance customers in finance referenceable?
[06:25] Jared: We have several banking customers we can reference—signature references available under NDA. We'll include a short list in the follow-up.
[06:33] Maria: Can we run an initial proof-of-concept in eu-west-1 with 2 endpoints and a limited token budget just to validate latency and log flow?
[06:40] Jared: Yes, that's our recommended next step. we'll propose a 4 week pilot on Dedicated in eu-west-1 with two reserved instances, and we can provide a security checklist.
[06:50] Raj: On legal — any concerns about subprocessor list and data export? we need complete subprocessor transparency.
[06:56] Priya: We'll provide the subprocessor list and can include contractual clauses for notification on changes. We also have a process for subprocessor audits for enterprise customers.
[07:07] Ellen: Operational runbook — if something goes wrong, how are incidents surfaced? we need incident escalation into our oncall and a phone bridge for Sev 1.
[07:16] Liam: We have an escalation path with SLOs, a dedicated TAM for enterprise tiers, and direct pager escalation for Sev 1; we'll share an example runbook and oncall contact template.
[07:27] Maria: One tangent — are LLM model weights considered a "backup" of data that needs residency controls? i ask because caching may persist some user content in model cache.
[07:36] Priya: Model weights are not customer data; KV caches might store context to speed responses. We treat KV cache as ephemeral and can scope cache residency. For strict residency, disable cross-region cache replicas and use local cache pinned to region.
[07:52] Tom: Performance question — if we do Dedicated with mTLS and VPC peering, do we lose throughput vs Hosted?
[07:59] Priya: Slightly higher cold-start latency due to isolated infra but sustained throughput is predictable. Dedicated gives consistent p99 latency, and our kernel selection optimizations still apply.
[08:10] Raj: For auditors, we need explicit language that logs containing identifiers are redacted within X minutes — do you have SLAs like that?
[08:18] Jared: We can contractually set retention windows and purge timelines for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted it's more nuanced but can be negotiated at enterprise tier.
[08:28] Ellen: Can you ingest logs directly into our SIEM with a push model? we want to own the canonical log copy.
[08:33] Priya: Yes, we support push to S3, SSE-KMS, and direct ingestion into Splunk/Datadog via secure connectors. For Dedicated we can stream logs in near real-time.
[08:45] Maria: Any automation around redaction policy testing? we'd like to run tests against sample transcripts to verify scrubbers.
[08:51] Priya: We can spin up a staging Dedicated pilot where you run your scrubber in-path. We'll include a test harness and sample redaction reports.
[09:01] Tom: Cost — any rule of thumb difference between Hosted and Dedicated?
[09:06] Jared: Dedicated has a higher base cost but lower per-token marginal cost for large volumes. We'll send a cost model. For your scale a 3-month reserved pilot typically pays back if you cross X tokens per month; we'll calculate in the follow-up.
[09:19] Raj: About legal — data subject requests: if an EU user asks for deletion, is Redwood able to delete all copies including backups?
[09:26] Priya: We can delete primary and nearline copies within the agreed purge timeframe; long-term backups may have retention but we can isolate and exclude customer data from long-term backups in Dedicated/Private. We'll include the deletion flow diagram.
[09:40] Ellen: Are there any gotchas in model updates that might cause data movement across regions? e.g., during rollout or retraining.
[09:47] Priya: We do not train on customer data unless explicitly contracted. Model updates are controlled and tested; deployment rollouts can be region-specific. We'll include a note on code paths that touch cache migration.
[09:58] Maria: ok, sounds promising. recap of agreed items?
[10:02] Jared: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2/HIPAA docs, subprocessor list, sample audit logs, Dedicated pilot pricing for eu-west-1 with options for BYOK/HSM, and a timeline to set up a PKI call. Argentum to share internal retention policy and any example PII patterns for scrubber testing.
[10:18] Raj: we'll also send a redline of our standard data processing addendum for review.
[10:22] Jared: Great. we'll target the next call the week of Nov 9 for the PKI deep dive. Thanks all.
[10:28] Maria: Thanks everyone.
